problem: VLN pretraining objectives that generate actions (PREVALENT, HAMT) depend on costly human-annotated instruction-action pairs, so they don't scale. Web image-text pretraining, by contrast, never connects representations to action generation.
motivation: VLN suffers from limited training data and poor generalization to unseen environments. An agent can explore environments by itself and collect paths at almost no cost, so a self-supervised objective built on those paths could scale while still training conditional action generation.
key_idea: Have the agent randomly explore environments, collect paths, and pretrain it to reconstruct the full path from a masked subpath (25% of viewpoints) that replaces the language instruction.
insight: MPM acts as a VLN-like task whose 'instruction' is a masked path, so it can be trained on self-collected data. Its gains are largest on path-fidelity metrics (CLS/nDTW/sDTW) on long-horizon R4R and RxR, since reconstructing the original path favors faithful following over shortest-path shortcuts. Ablations show that matching path lengths to the target dataset helps (R4R paths: sDTW 35.50 vs 33.92 with R2R paths on R4R). Using MPM in both pretraining and finetuning is generally best. Running MPM on the unseen test environments beforehand gives a further gain (R4R SR 46.88 -> 51.34), suggesting it can scale.
method: Base model: HAMT-style history-aware transformer (text encoder, hierarchical history ViT, panoramic observation ViT, dual-stream cross-modal transformer), with a frozen CLIP-ViT-L/14-336 vision encoder instead of ImageNet features (the HAMT+ baseline).
Active path collection: the agent random-walks over viewpoints with uniform choice and no revisits; path lengths are sampled to follow the length distribution of the training data.

MPM objective: mask 25% of viewpoints in a collected path and feed only the front-facing view features at the remaining viewpoints, through a linear projection, to the cross-modal transformer in place of the instruction. The agent is trained by imitation learning to reproduce the original action sequence.

Parameter sharing: MPM and VLN share all parameters. MPM is added to pretraining alongside MLM, ITM, SAP/SAR and SPREL (MRM is dropped because of CLIP), and to finetuning with equal loss weights alongside IL+A3C RL.
Pre-exploration variant (MPM-Prexplore): additionally run MPM on the unseen val environments with no instructions before testing.

setting.backbone: HAMT-style transformer (9-layer text, 2-layer panoramic, 4-layer cross-modal) with frozen CLIP-ViT-L/14-336; BERT for R2R/R4R, XLM-R for RxR
setting.training_data: R2R/R4R/RxR training data plus self-collected random-walk paths in the training environments; R2R also uses the PREVALENT augmented data (Hong et al. 2021). No augmented data for the other datasets. Pretraining 200k iterations, finetuning 300k iterations.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views, CLIP features) plus relative heading/elevation angle features
setting.privileged: none (except in the Prexplore analysis, where the agent explores the test environments beforehand)

numbers.extra: uses augmented R2R data; greedy single-run

results: Adding MPM to the stronger CLIP-based HAMT+ baseline raises val-unseen SR on R2R from 67.05 to 68.37, on R4R from 44.75 to 46.88, and on RxR from 62.00 to 63.51. Pre-exploring the unseen environments with MPM gives further gains, for example R2R SR 69.60 and R4R SR 51.34.
limitations: Gains over the HAMT+ baseline are modest (about 1-2 SR points), and the model is selected on val-unseen.
Paths come from naive random walks with length matching, and no more sophisticated exploration strategies are tried.
Large-scale MPM pretraining is not actually demonstrated; only a small-scale pre-exploration analysis is given, and it uses the test environments.
